rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi is reported to have claimed that a Prophetic report supports the weighing of deeds.
rows.anchor: وزعم الرازي على مانقل عنه أن فيه حديثا مرفوعا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Some say deeds themselves are weighed after righteous and sinful acts take luminous or dark forms, placed in corresponding pans; their weight reflects divine grace and justice.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون يوزن نفس الاعمال فتصور الصالحة بصور حسنة نورانية ثم تطرح في كفة النور

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others say God creates bodies equal in number to deeds, without transforming the deeds; they claim a transmitted report supports this.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب بعضهم إلى أن الله تعالى يخلق أجساما على عدد تلك الاعمال من غير قلب لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense compares weight and lightness to worldly gravity: heavy deeds descend before rising to Illiyyin, and light ones rise before falling to Sijjin; al-Qurtubi states this explicitly.
rows.anchor: والظاهر ان الثقل والخفة مثلها في الدنيا فما ثقل نزل

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: Some later scholars reverse worldly behavior: a believer's good deeds rise when they outweigh, while a disbeliever's pan is heavy because its other pan lacks good deeds; the author's cited proof is questionable.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المتأخرين هما على خلاف مافي الدنيا وأن عمل المؤمن اذا رجح صعد وثقلت سيآته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One account says all deeds are placed on the scales at once, with good deeds in a luminous right pan toward Paradise and sins in a dark pan toward Hell; God gives each person necessary knowledge of their relative weight.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن صفة الوزن أن يجعل جميع أعمال العباد في الميزان مرة واحدة الحسنات في كفة النور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A related account says a luminous column from the good-deed pan covering the other pan signals preponderance, while a dark column from the sin pan covering the good pan signals lightness.
rows.anchor: وقيل نحوه الا ان علامة الرجحان عمود من نور يثور من كفة الحسنات

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says not everyone is weighed: some enter Paradise without reckoning, while sinners may instead be identified by their marks and seized; weighing remains for those God wills.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي لايكون في حق كل أحد لما في الحديث الصحيح فيقال يامحمد أدخل الجنة من أمتك من لاحساب عليهم

rows.speaker: القاضي منذر بن سعيد البلوطي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Mundhir ibn Sa'id al-Baluti says the patient are not weighed; their reward is poured out to them.
rows.anchor: وذكر القاضي منذر بن سعيد البلوطي أن أهل الصبر لاتوزن أعمالهم وانما يصب لهم الأجر صبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite apparently falls under the disbeliever, but the author holds that everyone's deeds are weighed, based on the plain sense of many verses and reports; the intended weighing is beneficial weighing.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه يدرج المنافق في الكافر والحق أن أعمالهم مطلقا توزن لظواهر الآيات والاحاديث الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing and unbelieving jinn are subject to weighing just like humans; the distinctions described concern only those whose deeds are weighed.
rows.anchor: والصحيح ان الجن مؤمنهم وكافرهم كالانس في هذا الشأن

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites deny that the scales are literal.
rows.anchor: وأنكر المعتزلة الوزن حقيقة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والاعمش
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-A'mash say deeds are accidents that cannot be weighed; the scales instead represent just judgment.
rows.anchor: منهم مجاهد والضحاك والاعمش قالوا ان الاعمال أعراض ان أمكن بقاؤها لايمكن وزنها فالوزن عبارة عن القضاء السوي والحكم العادل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra allows mawazin to mean weighed things: deeds that have weight and standing with God; their heaviness means their measure outweighs.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا فيما هنا أن تكون الموازين جمع موزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light scales mean either that a person has no good deed of consequence or that sins outweigh good deeds.
rows.anchor: بان لم يكن له حسنة يعتد بها أو ثقلت سيآته على حسناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-lahw originally means heedlessness, then broadened to anything that occupies someone; customary usage narrows it to a pleasurable distraction near play, while here it makes people heedless.
rows.anchor: وأصل اللهو الغفلة ثم شاع في كل شاغل وخصه العرف بالشاغل الذي يسر المرء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines diversion as whatever distracts someone from what matters to them.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب اللهو مايشغلك عما يعني ويهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-takathur is competing and boasting over who has more, each group claiming numerical superiority.
rows.anchor: بأن يقول هؤلاء نحن أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people counted all the living, then turned to the graves and counted their dead; the endpoint is included in the distraction, and the occasion of revelation explains the image.
rows.anchor: حتى اذا استوعبتم عدد الأحياء صرتم إلى المقابر وانتقلتم إلى ذكر من فيها فتكاثرتم بالاموات

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm competed in numbers; after Abd Manaf first prevailed, Sahm counted the dead too and claimed victory.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي ومقاتل أن بني عبد مناف وبني سهم تفاخروا أيهم أكثر عددا فكثرتهم بنو عبد مناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reported contest, visiting graves means reaching the point of mentioning the dead, figuratively or by metonymy; the author favors treating it as a representation.
rows.anchor: وزيارة المقابر على ماتقدم على ظاهلها وأما على هذا فقد عبر بها عن بلوغهم ذكر الموتى كناية أو مجازا واستحسن جعله تمثيلا

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reads the grave-visiting expression as mockery of the competitors.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف عبر ذلك عما ذكر تهكما بهم

rows.speaker: بعض
rows.claim: One explanation of the mockery likens them to someone visiting graves without a sound purpose.
rows.anchor: ووجهه بعض بأنه كانه قيل أنتم في فعلكم هذا كمن يزور القبور من غير غرض صحيح

rows.speaker: بعض آخر
rows.claim: Another explanation, which the author prefers, says grave visits should prompt reflection on death, but these people turned them into a cause of heedlessness.
rows.anchor: وبعض آخر بأن زيارة القبور للاتعاظ وتذكر الموت وهم عكسوا فجعلوها سببا للغفلة وهذا أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivalry distracted people from the religious duty that truly matters; omitting the object of distraction magnifies the reproach through ambiguity and emphasizes the blame.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ألهاكم ذلك وهو لايعنيكم ولا يجدي عليكم في دنياكم وآخرتكم عما يعنيكم من أمر الدين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An alternative reading says wealth and children distracted people until death and burial; Ibn Abbas is cited for this interpretation, with al-Hasan also reported by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Abi Shayba.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد ألهاكم التكاثر بالاموال والاولاد إلى أن متم وقبرتم

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: Poetry uses visiting the grave as an expression for dying, supporting the interpretation of grave visitation as death.
rows.anchor: ذاق الضماد أو يزور القبرا

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir likewise uses grave visitation for death, saying Abu Malik visited the graves and became their most ignoble visitor.
rows.anchor: وقال جرير زار القبور أبو مالك فاصبح ألأم زوارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression points to resurrection; an Arab reportedly inferred that the people must be raised for Judgment, since a visitor departs rather than remains.
rows.anchor: يحكي أن اعرابيا سمع ذلك فقال بعث القوم للقيامة ورب الكعبة

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says every visitor must return to either Paradise or Hell, also suggesting a short stay in the graves.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز انه قال لابد لمن زار أن يرجع إلى جنة أو نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense indicates certainty, the predominance of those who died first, or treating the deaths of ancestors as their own.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالماضي لتحقق الوقوع أو لتغلب من مات أولا أو لجعل موت آبائهم بمنزلة موتهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says God will reproach the disbelievers with this surah on Judgment Day, after they have visited graves; the author calls this astonishing.
rows.anchor: قول أبي مسلم ان الله عز وجل يتكلم بهذه السورة يوم القيامة تعييرا للكفار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A different interpretation rebukes excessive grave-visiting done to boast about predecessors; the author says the verse is far from that meaning and instead affirms visits for remembering the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقيل هذا تأنيب على الاكثار من زيارة القبور تكثرا بمن سلف ومباهاة وتفاخرا به لااتعاظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author condemns boasting over graves and the associated abuses of some ignorant Sufis, while recognizing grave-visiting for admonition as prescribed.
rows.anchor: في ذم زيارة القبور للتفاخر بالمزور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة
rows.claim: These readers lengthen the initial alif in alhakum, making the phrase interrogative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعائشة ومعاوية وأبو عمران الجوني وأبو صالح ومالك بن دينار وأبو الجوزاء وجماعة آلهاكم بالمد

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وابن عباس والشعبي وأبي العالية وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي
rows.claim: A transmission from these readers has two hamzas at the start, also forming an interrogative for confirmation.
rows.anchor: وروى عن أبي بكر الصديق رضى الله عنه وابن عباس أيضا والشعبي وابي العالية وأبن أبي عبلة والكسائي في رواية أألهاكم بهمزتين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the oath is by the Asr prayer because of its virtue; the majority identify it as the middle prayer, supported by reports naming it and warning against missing it.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل أقسم سبحانه بصلاة العصر لفضلها لانها الصلاة الوسطى عند الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author dismisses a story about a sinful woman being told her gravest sin was missing Asr prayer as unreliable material from an otherwise prominent transmitter.
rows.anchor: ذكر ذلك الامام وهو لعمري امام في نقل مثل ذلك مما لايعول عليه عند أئمة الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asr prayer is especially meritorious because people neglect it while absorbed in trade and work late in the day.
rows.anchor: وخصت بالفضل لان التكليف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the oath is by the time of the Asr prayer, or by the creation of Adam on Friday; he also explains al-asr as evening, rich in signs of divine power like dawn.
rows.anchor: وقيل أقسم عز وجل بوقت تلك الصلاة لفضيلة صلاته أو لخلق آدم أبي البشر عليه السلام فيه من يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says al-asr means day or night, and cites Hamid ibn Thawr's verse about the two spans of time, day and night.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج العصر اليوم والعصر الليلة وعليه قول حميد بن ثور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some interpret al-asr as morning and evening, the two cool periods; on this and the preceding view the oath is to one of two unspecified times.
rows.anchor: وقيل العصر بكرة والعصر عشية وهما الابرادان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take al-asr as the Prophet's era or his lifetime through the Resurrection, whose remaining span is compared in a Bukhari report to the time from Asr to sunset; its honor comes from the Prophet and his community.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به عصر النبوة وكأنه عنى به وقت حياته عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-asr is time itself, encompassing wonders and blessings as well as their opposites; the oath warns people facing ruin or salvation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس هو الدهر أقسم عز وجل به لاشتماله على أصناف العجائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath honors time while denying that time itself causes loss or events, as some claim; attributing loss to humanity shows it is a human quality, not a defect of time.
rows.anchor: ويعرض عز وجل لما في الاقسام به من التعظيم بنفي أن يكون له خسران أو دخل فيه كما يزعمه من يضيف الحوادث اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that using al-asr to mean time in general is not linguistically apparent.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بان استعمال العصر بذلك المعنى غير ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is in loss through its ventures, efforts, and lifetimes spent on aims that do not benefit in the afterlife and may harm them.
rows.anchor: أي خسران في متاجرهم ومساعيهم وصرف أعمارهم في مباغيهم التي لاينتفعون بها في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in loss is comprehensive because of the exception that follows; the indefinite form either magnifies the loss or identifies a kind humans do not recognize.
rows.anchor: والتعريف للاستغراق بقرينة الاستثناء والتنكير قيل للتعظيم

rows.speaker: علي ومحمد بن الحنيفة وابن عباس وابن عمر وزيد بن أسلم والضحاك وعكرمة
rows.claim: These authorities interpret al-ma'un as zakat; al-Ra'i's poetry is also cited in support.
rows.anchor: أي الزكاة كما جاء عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابنه محمد بن الحنيفة وابن عباس وابن عمر

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب والكلبي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b and al-Kalbi are cited for interpreting al-ma'un as customary helpfulness or a common good.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب والكلبي المعروف

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud interprets al-ma'un as household items people lend one another, such as a cooking pot or axe; a report from Ibn Abbas is also cited by al-Diya and al-Hakim, who authenticated it.
rows.anchor: وأخرج جماعة عن ابن أبي مسعود تفسيره بما يتعاوره الناس بينهم من القدر والفاس ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Refusing to lend such things can be forbidden when someone is in need and blameworthy in good manners when there is no necessity; several Prophetic reports support the interpretation.
rows.anchor: ومنع ذلك قد يكون محضورا في الشريعة كما اذا استعير عن اضطرار وقبيحا في المرؤة

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri, in a report transmitted by Ibn Abi Shayba, says al-ma'un means wealth in Quraysh usage.
rows.anchor: وعلى ما أخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن الزهري المال بلسان قريش

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج والمبرد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda, al-Zajjaj, and al-Mubarrad say the word covered every useful thing, small or large, in pre-Islamic usage, and means obedience in Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة والزجاج وامبرد هو في الجاهلية كل مافيه منفعة من قليل أو كثير

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub derives al-ma'un from ma'n, meaning a small thing, as in the expression for possessing only a little.
rows.anchor: فقال قطرب أصله فاعول من المعن وهو الشيء القليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another derivation makes al-ma'un come from ma'una, with the alif replacing the final h and the original form on the maf'al pattern.
rows.anchor: وقيل أصله معونة والالف عوض عن الهاء فوزنه مفعل في الاصل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third derivation treats it as the passive participle of a'ana, with consonant inversion and a later change of waw to alif.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو اسم مفعول من أعان يعين وأصله معوون فقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in fa-wayl marks consequence and the discourse escalates: if abandoning the orphan and failing to urge feeding are bad, neglecting prayer, showing off, and withholding zakat or even common loans are worse.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله تعالى فويل الخ جزائية والكلام ترق من ذلك المعرف إلى معرف أقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These vices characterize those who deny Judgment, so believers must avoid them; denial of the religion is the root of every sin.
rows.anchor: والغرض التغليظ في أمر هذه الرذائل التي ابتلى بها كثير من الناس وانها لما كانت من سيماء المكذب بالدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report identifies the person as Abu Jahl, who was guardian to an orphan but harshly drove away the unclothed child when he asked for his own property.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو أبو جهل وكان وصيا ليتيم فأتاه عرياتا يأله من مال نفسه فدفعه دفعا شنيعا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the person as Abu Sufyan: after slaughtering camels, he struck an orphan with his stick when the child asked for meat.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج وهو أبو سفيان نحر جزروا فسأله يتيم لحما فقرعه بعصاه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other identifications are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Wa'il, Amr ibn A'id, Manaf, or a miserly hypocrite.
rows.anchor: وقيل الوليد بن المغيرة وقيل العاص بن وائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kashf objects that making the prayer neglecters and show-offs the same defined person does not fit; the author instead reads this as a parenthetical extension from abandoning the orphan to worse conduct.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشف غير ملائم بل يكون شبه استطراد مستفاد من الوصف المعرف اعنى دع اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage asks whether deniers and orphan-abandoners behave well or badly, answers that their behavior is bad, then says woe to the praying people to show that they too share these traits.
rows.anchor: فكانه قبل أخبرني ماتقول فيمن يكذبون بالدين وفيمن يؤذن اليتيم أحسن حالهم ومايصنعون أم قبح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some make the fa in fa-wayl causal, which requires the deniers and praying people to be one group; this supports identifying them as hypocrites, as reported from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Imam Malik.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعضهم الفاء في فويل على العطف المذكور للسببية وهذا الوجه يقتضي اتحاد المصلين والمكذبين

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that the proposed coordination is an unusual construction and that the demonstrative pronoun is awkward and unnecessary, though another says it stresses their remoteness in evil.
rows.anchor: وأعترض أبو حيان ذلك الوجه بأن التركيب عليه تركيب غريب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another analysis coordinates two groups as separate subjects, but al-Kashf objects that the context does not suit a pronoun referring jointly to both and then being replaced by the praying people.
rows.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون العطف عطف ذات على ذات فالاستخبار عن حال المكذبين وحال الداعين

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق والأشهب
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and al-Ashhab read yara'una with a short vowel and a doubled hamza; another transmission from Ibn Ishaq shortens it without doubling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن إسحاق والاشهب يرؤون بالقصر وتشديد الهمزة

rows.speaker: البقاعي
rows.claim: Al-Biqa'i also calls al-Kawthar Surat al-Nahr; reports differ between Meccan and Medinan origin, with al-Itqan and al-Nawawi preferring the Medinan view.
rows.anchor: وتسملى كما قال البقاعي سورة النحر

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet awoke smiling and announced the revelation of a surah, then recited al-Kawthar; this report is cited in support of its Medinan origin.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال أغفى رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم اغفاءة فرفع رأسه متبسما

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji says one author resolved the disagreement about the surah's origin by arguing that it was revealed twice.
rows.anchor: وذكر الخفاجي أن لبعضهم تأليفا صحح فيه أنها نزلت مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has three verses by consensus and is described as the Quran's shortest surah; the Imam reads it as a precise counterpart to the preceding surah's four traits of the hypocrite.
rows.anchor: وآيها ثلاث بلا خوف وليس في القرآن كما أخرج البيهقي عن ابن شبرمة سورة آيها أقل من ذلك

rows.speaker: الامام
rows.claim: The gift of abundant good answers miserliness; al-kawthar counters the hypocrite's withholding.
rows.anchor: لان السابقة وصف الله تعالى فيها المنافق بأربعة أمور البخل وترك الصلاة

rows.speaker: الامام
rows.claim: The command to pray counters neglect of prayer, and praying for one's Lord counters showing off for people.
rows.anchor: وفي مقابلة ترك الصلاة فصل أي دم على الصلاة وفي مقابلة الرياء لربك أي لرضاه لا للناس

rows.speaker: الامام
rows.claim: Sacrifice counters withholding al-ma'un, understood here as giving charity from sacrificial meat.
rows.anchor: وفي مقابلة منع الماعون وانحر وأراد به سبحانه التصدق بلحوم الاضاحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night as it yasri means as it moves away or departs, as in the verse about the night when it departs.
rows.anchor: أي إذا سار وذهب كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it means when night arrives and comes on; the intended sense is every night.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : إذا جاء وأقبل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة والكلبي
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ikrima, and al-Kalbi identify it as the night of Muzdalifa.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة والكلبي : هي ليلة المزدلفة

rows.speaker: قراء أهل الحجاز والبصرة
rows.claim: Readers in the Hijaz and Basra pronounce the final ya in yasri when continuing; Ibn Kathir and Ya'qub also retain it when pausing, while the rest omit it in both positions.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز ،   والبصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ya is omitted to preserve the rhyme endings, but retained by others because it is the root letter and verbs do not normally lose it at a pause.
rows.anchor: فمن حذف فلوفاق رؤوس الآي

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the missing ya by saying the night does not itself travel; people travel in it, so the verb is treated as diverted from its ordinary sense.
rows.anchor: وسئل الأخفش عن العلة في سقوط الياء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash compares the inflectional reduction to Maryam 19:28, where baghiy is used instead of baghiyya because the word is treated as shortened from baghiya.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل : بغية لأنها صرفت من باغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and has ten verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الضحى مكية وآياتها عشرة

rows.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
rows.claim: Jundub ibn Sufyan reports that after the Prophet was ill and did not rise for two or three nights, a woman taunted him that his Satan had left; then the opening verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: سمعت جندب بن سفيان قال : " اشتكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report identifies the woman who taunted the Prophet as Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن المرأة التي قالت ذلك أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say Jews asked the Prophet about Dhul-Qarnayn, the Companions of the Cave, and the Spirit; after he promised an answer the next day without saying God willing, revelation stopped.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون " سألت اليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Gabriel's delay was caused by a puppy in the Prophet's house; Gabriel explained that angels do not enter a house containing a dog or image.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم : كان سبب احتباس جبريل عليه السلام عنه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Reports disagree about the duration of the revelation's delay: Ibn Jurayj says twelve days, Ibn Abbas fifteen, and Muqatil forty.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن جريج : اثنا عشر يوماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When polytheists said God had abandoned and hated Muhammad, the surah was revealed; the Prophet said he missed Gabriel, who replied that he too yearned but was only a commanded servant.
rows.anchor: فقال المشركون : إن محمداً ودعه ربه وقلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation concludes with God's statement that angels descend only by their Lord's command.
rows.anchor: فأنزل : { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-duha can mean the whole day, since it is paired with the night; the verse about punishment arriving duha likewise means daytime.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالضحى وأراد به النهار كله

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatada and Muqatil instead interpret al-duha as the specific late-morning period, when the sun has risen and the day is temperate across seasons.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل : يعني وقت الضحى
